title: Purity of $H_c^2$ on an affine curve
statement:
Let $U_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine curve and let
$\mathcal F$ be a lisse Weil sheaf on $U_0$ which is punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $w$. Then $H_c^2(U,\mathcal F)$, with its
Frobenius, is $\iota$-pure of weight $w+2$ in the sense of
[def-weil-frobenius-module-weights] (the zero module being pure of
every weight).

proof.text: Put $U=U_0\times_{k_0}k$, $V=\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}$ and $W=V_{\pi_1(U)}$. Apply [lem-a1-affine-hc2] to the given smooth geometrically connected affine curve and lisse Weil sheaf: it supplies a Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism $e:H_c^2(U,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim}W(-1)$. In particular the Frobenius used below is the one on this cohomology group, not a local Frobenius at an arbitrary closed point of $U_0$.

The nonempty smooth geometrically connected curve $U_0$ and the given punctually pure lisse Weil sheaf satisfy exactly the hypotheses of [lem-a1-geometric-coinvariants-pure]. Thus $(W,F_W)$ is pure of weight $w$. The current blueprint version of that lemma defines $W=\Gamma(U,\mathcal F^\vee)^\vee$ and explicitly identifies it, when $U$ is connected as here, with $V_{\pi_1(U)}$ with induced Frobenius. Hence it is the same Frobenius quotient as in step 1; there is no assumption of semisimplicity.

source.place: second paragraph: purity of the coinvariants

proof.text: Apply [lem-wf-tate-twist-frobenius] with $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$, its unique closed point, and $m=-1$: $Q_x=q$, so the finite-coefficient-field Tate line $E(-1)$ has Frobenius $q$. The global-point and scalar-extension statement [lem-pur-twist-frobenius-scalar] gives the same multiplication by $q$ on the one-dimensional $\Qlb(-1)$. By the tensor Frobenius formula of [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists], choosing a nonzero vector $t$ in that line identifies $W(-1)$ with $W$ by $v\otimes t\mapsto v$, and its Frobenius with $qF_W$: $F(v\otimes t)=F_W(v)\otimes qt$. This uses the rank-one line and its specified Frobenius, without asserting that a choice of basis is canonical.

source.place: third paragraph: geometric Frobenius on the Tate line and tensor action

proof.text:
For an eigenvalue $ eta$ of $qF_W$ choose a nonzero eigenvector $v$. Since $q
e0$, the equation $qF_Wv= eta v$ is equivalent to $F_Wv=( eta/q)v$. Step 2 and [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights] therefore give $|\iota( eta/q)|=q^{w/2}$. As $\iota$ fixes the positive rational integer $q$, multiplicativity of the complex absolute value gives $|\iota( eta)|=q\,q^{w/2}=q^{1+w/2}=q^{(w+2)/2}$. If $h
e0$ is an eigenvector in $H_c^2$ then $e(h)
e0$ and Frobenius equivariance makes it an eigenvector of the same eigenvalue in $W(-1)$; hence this bound is precisely purity of $H_c^2$ of weight $w+2$. If $W=0$, step 1 gives $H_c^2=0$ and there are no eigenvalues, so the same definition proves purity of every weight.

source.place: third paragraph: explicit eigenvector and absolute-value calculation

proof_origin.place: all three paragraphs; expanded tensor action and eigenvector calculation

The statement matches main-20261015 lem-a1-affine-hc2-pure.md verbatim and is not weakened, and there are no new nodes. Step 1: lem-a1-affine-hc2 has the same hypotheses as the item (smooth, geometrically connected, affine curve; lisse Weil sheaf), and the step takes only its stated Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism H_c^2 ≅ V_{π1(U)}(-1). Step 2: the hypotheses of lem-a1-geometric-coinvariants-pure hold in both the original and the blueprint_update version. U_0 is nonempty because it is geometrically connected, and it is separated and of finite type as def-wf-fundamental-representation requires. The update identifies Γ(U,F^∨)^∨ with V_{π1(U)} with its induced Frobenius, so F_W is the same operator in both steps. Step 3: lem-wf-tate-twist-frobenius at X_0 = Spec k_0 with m = -1 gives q on E(-1). lem-pur-twist-frobenius-scalar gives the same scalar after extending to Qbar_l, so the change of coefficients is cited rather than silently assumed. The Frobenius of the twist comes from the tensor formula in clause 5 of def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists, which gives Frobenius qF_W on W(-1). Step 4 is genuinely elementary: an eigenvector calculation under the definition of weights, the transport of eigenvectors along the equivariant isomorphism, and the case W = 0. I tested the constant sheaf, a geometrically constant rank-one sheaf (eigenvalue qα), a sheaf with W = 0, a non-semisimple Frobenius, and a curve with no rational point; all are consistent. proof_deps equals the union of the uses, every cited id exists, there is no cycle, and no SGA source is cited.
